result.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
result.summary: We demonstrate that transformer architectures trained with discrete denoising diffusion and decoded via guided test-time beam search can learn to recover the prime factors of semiprime integers directly from data. Our approach establishes a new frontier for learning-based semiprime factorization, successfully factoring 68-bit integers-a substantial advance over the prior 56-bit state of the art. While computationally less efficient than classical factoring algorithms, our model requires no domain-specific number-theoretic priors and learns purely from training examples. In practice, the diffusion model acts as a generative prior, identifying promising factor candidates where exact verification or lattice-based post-processing can complete the factorization. Furthermore, we derive empirical scaling laws relating approximation quality to training data volume, model size, and test-time computation. In contrast to language, problem size is the key driver of scaling behavior. Achieving a fixed accuracy on a held-out test set requires compute that scales exponentially with bit length. Consequently, our findings pose no threat to security, as the projected compute cost required to factorize cryptographically relevant integers remains prohibitive.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用离散去噪扩散 Transformer 配合引导式测试时 beam search，从训练样本直接学习半素数分解，将成功分解位数推进到 68 位，并给出精度随数据量、模型规模和测试时计算变化的经验 scaling law。
AI.relevance_reason: 「扩散生成候选因子 + 束搜索与精确验证补全」的流程可供核查 LVR 中生成与验证的分工、测试时计算的分配与停止判据，其按问题规模的经验 scaling 也可能类比 latent 长度泛化；但无视觉与多模态成分，迁移需较多推断。
